dedupe_keys.name: disaster debris management after hurricanes helene and milton florida 2024 32 stakeholder interviews on barriers and supports ijdrr 2026

description: This study examines how debris from Hurricanes Helene and Milton was cleared in Florida in 2024, when the two storms struck 14 days apart. The abstract read on 2026-09-28, by Najiba Rashid and Jenna Tilt in the International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction, reports 32 semi-structured interviews with municipal, county, state and federal officials and with debris haulers and monitors about what hindered and helped debris management. Coverage is Florida after the 2024 hurricane season. The findings name capacity limits as the most pervasive barrier, namely shortages of equipment, trucks, labour and pre-permitted temporary debris management sites, worsened by the short gap between the storms, and credit pre-event contracts, strategic permitting of temporary sites and strong communication between agencies with improving efficiency; the authors conclude that debris management is a governance challenge needing local capacity and clear coordination across levels of government. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-NC-4.0 (article). Caveats: the evidence is qualitative, with no debris volumes or clearance times in the abstract. It supports recovery and emergency response studies, such as setting truck and site capacity in debris clearance models for back-to-back hurricanes. Related records: Florida hurricane marine debris lessons and the CRS report on disaster debris management. Access is through the provider page linked in this record.
